main_body: A wooden baby cradle seen from the side (end-on): a tall headboard at the left with a light cream pillow, a low basin with blue blanket at the right, and rocker feet below.
top_band: none as a distinct band: the headboard cap is a 1-2 row tan rim at rows 3-4, and the basin rim is a thin tan line at rows 7-9. The blue blanket is a small patch.
evidence: The cradle is drawn as an end-on profile. A column through the middle of the main body meets a 1-2 row tan rim, then a brown front/side face. The pillow and blanket are small, and the bed interior is not a clear horizontal surface with a front edge line and a shaded face below. There is no eave shadow and no inset front. This matches the side elevation chair/cradle failure in the guide, because no horizontal surface reads clearly from above.

style.evidence: The cradle is tiny, with about 3 wood tones (tan, mid brown, dark brown) plus a light blue blanket and a cream pillow. The outline is a dark brown, tinted toward the wood, so it is not a sticker look. The surfaces have little grain or speckle, and the tiles carry about 3-5 colours each, well below the stall and well references, which have 5-6 steps per material and rich texture. It looks thinner and flatter next to the reference.
